english: don't you think?; don't you agree?
use: Tags your opinion and invites agreement; answer sou da ne to agree or u-n, dou kana to hedge.

example.romaji: ano eiga, nagasugita yo. sou omowanai?
example.ja: あの映画、長すぎたよ。そう思わない？
example.english: That film was way too long. Don't you think?

examplePolite.romaji: ano eiga, chotto nagakatta desu yo ne. sou omoimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: あの映画、ちょっと長かったですよね。そう思いませんか？
examplePolite.english: That film was a bit long. Don't you think?

notes: Asked in the negative but means 'you agree, right?', so un means you agree.

polite: jissai dou na n desu ka?
english: what's it really like?; how is it, honestly?
use: Asks for the real story behind a reputation: a job, a city, a relationship.

example.romaji: toukyou no seikatsu tte, jissai dou na no?
example.ja: 東京の生活って、実際どうなの？
example.english: So what's life in Tokyo really like?

examplePolite.romaji: toukyou no seikatsu tte, jissai dou na n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 東京の生活って、実際どうなんですか？
examplePolite.english: So what's life in Tokyo really like?

notes: Jissai means 'in reality'; jissai wa ... (actually, ...) introduces the truth.

english: so what did you think?; your thoughts?
use: Asked right after someone has seen, read, tried or done something; answer with a one-line verdict.

example.romaji: ano hon, yomiowatta? de, kansou wa?
example.ja: あの本、読み終わった？で、感想は？
example.english: Did you finish that book? So, what did you think?

examplePolite.romaji: ano hon, yomiowarimashita ka? kansou wa dou desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: あの本、読み終わりましたか？感想はどうですか？
examplePolite.english: Did you finish that book? What did you think?

notes: Kansou means 'impressions' of an experience; a view on an issue is iken.

kana: どっちがいいとおもう？
polite: dochira ga ii to omoimasu ka?
politeJa: どちらがいいと思いますか？
english: which do you think is better?
use: Asks a friend to help you choose between two things: clothes, dates, plans.

example.romaji: kono futatsu, dotchi ga ii to omou?
example.ja: この二つ、どっちがいいと思う？
example.english: Which of these two do you think is better?

examplePolite.romaji: kono futatsu, dochira ga ii to omoimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: この二つ、どちらがいいと思いますか？
examplePolite.english: Which of these two do you think is better?

notes: Dotchi is casual for dochira; for three or more options ask dore ga ii?

english: is it a nice place to live?; is it easy to live there?
use: Asked of someone who lives in a city, area or country you're curious about.

example.romaji: oosaka tte sumiyasui? bukka wa dou?
example.ja: 大阪って住みやすい？物価はどう？
example.english: Is Osaka a nice place to live? What are prices like?

examplePolite.romaji: oosaka wa sumiyasui desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 大阪は住みやすいですか？
examplePolite.english: Is Osaka a nice place to live?

notes: -yasui after a verb stem means 'easy to': tsukaiyasui (easy to use), wakariyasui (easy to understand).

english: I'm really into ...; I'm hooked on ...
use: Says what you're obsessed with right now; ask back with saikin nani ni hamatteru?

example.romaji: saikin, kankoku dorama ni hamatteru n da.
example.ja: 最近、韓国ドラマにハマってるんだ。
example.english: I'm really into Korean dramas lately.

examplePolite.romaji: saikin, kankoku dorama ni hamatte iru n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 最近、韓国ドラマにハマっているんです。
examplePolite.english: I'm really into Korean dramas lately.

notes: Hamaru literally means 'to get stuck in'; it implies a recent, strong craze rather than a lasting like (suki).

polite: oshigoto wa nani o shite imasu ka?
politeJa: お仕事は何をしていますか？
english: what do you do for work?
use: Asked when getting to know someone; people often answer by field, like kyouiku kankei (something in education).

example.romaji: ima shigoto nani shiteru no? mada ginkou?
example.ja: 今仕事何してるの？まだ銀行？
example.english: What are you doing for work now? Still at the bank?

examplePolite.romaji: shitsurei desu kedo, oshigoto wa nani o shite imasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 失礼ですけど、お仕事は何をしていますか？
examplePolite.english: If you don't mind me asking, what do you do for work?

kana: しゅうまつはだいたい〜
english: on weekends I usually ...
use: Answers shumi wa? or yasumi no hi nani shiteru?; finish with what you do, often in the -te iru form.

example.romaji: shuumatsu wa daitai ie de hiru made neteru.
example.ja: 週末はだいたい家で昼まで寝てる。
example.english: On weekends I mostly sleep in till noon.

examplePolite.romaji: shuumatsu wa daitai jimu ni itte imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 週末はだいたいジムに行っています。
examplePolite.english: On weekends I usually go to the gym.

notes: Daitai means 'mostly, roughly'; with numbers it's 'about': daitai sanzen en (about 3,000 yen).

kana: さいきんはじめたんだ
english: I only took it up recently; I just started
use: Said about a new hobby, often to excuse being bad at it.

example.romaji: gitaa wa saikin hajimeta n da. mada heta da yo.
example.ja: ギターは最近始めたんだ。まだ下手だよ。
example.english: I only took up guitar recently. I'm still bad.

examplePolite.romaji: gitaa wa saikin hajimeta n desu. mada heta desu.
examplePolite.ja: ギターは最近始めたんです。まだ下手です。
examplePolite.english: I only took up guitar recently. I'm still bad.

notes: Put the hobby first with wa: yoga wa saikin hajimeta n da.

src: 最近何か面白いの見た？
ja: 最近何か面白いの見た？
kana: さいきんなにかおもしろいのみた？
polite: saikin nanika omoshiroi no mimashita ka?
politeJa: 最近何か面白いの見ましたか？
english: seen anything good lately?
use: An easy conversation starter about films, shows or videos; answer with a title and a quick verdict.

example.romaji: nee, saikin nanika omoshiroi no mita? osusume aru?
example.ja: ねえ、最近何か面白いの見た？おすすめある？
example.english: Hey, seen anything good lately? Any recommendations?

examplePolite.romaji: saikin nanika omoshiroi no mimashita ka? osusume wa arimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 最近何か面白いの見ましたか？おすすめはありますか？
examplePolite.english: Seen anything good lately? Any recommendations?

notes: Omoshiroi covers both 'funny' and 'interesting'; the no stands in for 'thing'.

politeJa: あのニュース見ましたか？
english: did you see that news?; did you hear about that?
use: Opens a chat about a current story you both probably know about.

example.romaji: ne, kesa no ano nyuusu mita? bikkuri shita.
example.ja: ね、今朝のあのニュース見た？びっくりした。
example.english: Hey, did you see that news this morning? I was shocked.

examplePolite.romaji: kesa no ano nyuusu, mimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今朝のあのニュース、見ましたか？
examplePolite.english: Did you see that news this morning?

notes: Ano points to something you both know; use kono nyuusu when showing it on your phone.

kana: いまなにかドラマみてる？
polite: ima nanika dorama mite imasu ka?
politeJa: 今何かドラマ見ていますか？
english: are you watching any shows at the moment?
use: Small-talk opener; dorama covers any TV series, Japanese or foreign.

example.romaji: ima nanika dorama miteru? omoshiroi no oshiete.
example.ja: 今何かドラマ見てる？面白いの教えて。
example.english: Watching any shows right now? Tell me a good one.

examplePolite.romaji: saikin, nanika dorama o mite imasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 最近、何かドラマを見ていますか？
examplePolite.english: Are you watching any shows lately?

notes: Miteru is the spoken form of mite iru; the same works for reading: ima nanika yonderu?

english: who's your fave? (idol, band member, character)
use: Asked among fans of a group, show or anime; answer with a name plus ga oshi.

example.romaji: kono guruupu, oshi wa dare? watashi wa kono hito.
example.ja: このグループ、推しは誰？私はこの人。
example.english: Who's your fave in this group? Mine's this one.

examplePolite.romaji: kono guruupu de, oshi wa dare desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: このグループで、推しは誰ですか？
examplePolite.english: Who's your favourite in this group?

notes: From osu (to push, back); oshikatsu is fan activity like buying merch and going to shows.

kana: カラオケでなにうたう？
polite: karaoke de wa nani o utaimasu ka?
politeJa: カラオケでは何を歌いますか？
english: what do you sing at karaoke?
use: Asked when planning a karaoke night or getting to know someone's music taste.

example.romaji: kondo karaoke iku kedo, itsumo nani utau?
example.ja: 今度カラオケ行くけど、いつも何歌う？
example.english: We're doing karaoke soon. What do you usually sing?

examplePolite.romaji: karaoke de wa itsumo nani o utaimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: カラオケではいつも何を歌いますか？
examplePolite.english: What do you usually sing at karaoke?

notes: Your go-to song is your juuhachiban.

kana: からいのだいじょうぶ？
polite: karai no wa daijoubu desu ka?
politeJa: 辛いのは大丈夫ですか？
english: are you okay with spicy food?
use: Asked before ordering or cooking; answer daijoubu (fine) or chotto nigate (not great with it).

example.romaji: kimuchi nabe ni shiyou ka. karai no daijoubu?
example.ja: キムチ鍋にしようか。辛いの大丈夫？
example.english: Shall we get kimchi hotpot? Are you okay with spicy?

examplePolite.romaji: karai no wa daijoubu desu ka? kekkou karai desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 辛いのは大丈夫ですか？結構辛いですよ。
examplePolite.english: Are you okay with spicy food? It's pretty hot.

notes: Swap in any food: sakana daijoubu? (are you okay with fish?).

english: can you eat natto?
use: A classic question to foreigners about the sticky fermented beans; a yes usually gets a surprised reaction.

example.romaji: e, nattou taberareru no? sugoi ne.
example.ja: え、納豆食べられるの？すごいね。
example.english: Wait, you can eat natto? Impressive.

examplePolite.romaji: nattou wa taberaremasu ka? nigate na hito mo ooi desu kedo.
examplePolite.ja: 納豆は食べられますか？苦手な人も多いですけど。
examplePolite.english: Can you eat natto? Lots of people can't stand it.

notes: Taberareru means 'can eat'; it works for any food: sashimi taberareru?

english: I can't hold my drink; I'm a lightweight
use: Explains why you're drinking slowly or turning down a refill; the opposite is osake tsuyoi.

example.romaji: gomen, osake yowai n da. uuroncha ni suru.
example.ja: ごめん、お酒弱いんだ。ウーロン茶にする。
example.english: Sorry, I'm a lightweight. I'll have oolong tea.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, osake yowai n desu. uuroncha de.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、お酒弱いんです。ウーロン茶で。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, I can't hold my drink. Oolong tea for me.

notes: Osake means any alcohol, not just sake; osake wa nigate (not good with alcohol) also works.

src: お気に入りのお店ある？
ja: お気に入りのお店ある？
kana: おきにいりのおみせある？
polite: okiniiri no omise wa arimasu ka?
politeJa: お気に入りのお店はありますか？
english: got a favourite place to eat or hang out?
use: Asks for a local recommendation or about someone's regular spots.

example.romaji: kono hen de okiniiri no omise aru? oshiete.
example.ja: この辺でお気に入りのお店ある？教えて。
example.english: Got a favourite place around here? Tell me.

examplePolite.romaji: kono hen de okiniiri no omise wa arimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: この辺でお気に入りのお店はありますか？
examplePolite.english: Do you have a favourite place around here?

notes: Okiniiri means 'favourite'; ikitsuke no mise is 'my regular place'.

english: I'm more of a ... person, I guess
use: Answers a this-or-that question with your side; kana softens it.

example.romaji: watashi wa koohii yori koucha ha kana.
example.ja: 私はコーヒーより紅茶派かな。
example.english: I'm more of a tea person than coffee, I guess.

examplePolite.romaji: watashi wa koohii yori koucha ha desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 私はコーヒーより紅茶派ですね。
examplePolite.english: I'm more of a tea person than a coffee person.

notes: Ha (派) means 'camp, side' and is said ha, unlike the topic particle wa.

english: if anything; I'd lean toward; if I had to choose
use: Starts a mild preference when you're not strongly on either side.

example.romaji: dotchika tte iu to, natsu yori fuyu ga suki.
example.ja: どっちかっていうと、夏より冬が好き。
example.english: If anything, I prefer winter to summer.

examplePolite.romaji: dochira ka to iu to, natsu yori fuyu ga suki desu.
examplePolite.ja: どちらかと言うと、夏より冬が好きです。
examplePolite.english: If anything, I prefer winter to summer.

notes: Often ends with ... ha kana or ... no hou ga suki.
